title: THE ELDER WHO WOULD NOT LEAVE THE GRAVES
deck: A barn-sized slab is creeping toward the village of Kesk, and the oldest woman in it has locked herself in the burial ground; Illuminara learns what the refusal is guarding, and the village finds a way to carry it.
shape: Six scenes across one afternoon and the morning after: a rescue captain's three clocks, a walk along the rows of a burial ground, a plan made on a church porch, a reading of two hundred and fourteen names over a radio, a ledge crossed under a failing slab, and a frosted terrace where the first stone is set.

scenes.title: The Slab
paragraphs: *Kesk, the cliff track · noon*

The slab above Kesk was the size of a barn and had been moving for nine days. It moved the way a tired child leans on a door, so slowly that nobody could say when the leaning had stopped being a lean.

Captain Iven Roth of the valley rescue had called Illuminara himself, which she understood had cost him something. He did not shake her hand. He held out his tablet the way a man shows a doctor a wound he has already diagnosed.

**Roth**  
Two millimetres a day on Monday. Eleven an hour this morning. Plot one over the speed and the line walks down to zero at about eight tonight, give or take three hours. Rain is due at eight. I have been telling myself seven.

She laid her palm flat on the cliff beside the track and let the mountain show her where it was holding. The slab did not hang from the face. It leaned on a rock bridge behind it, a column the width of a bus, cracked through like a boiled bone and doing the work of the whole slope. She felt the load run down it the way you feel a pulse in a wrist.

**Illuminara**  
I can take the slab's weight off that bridge. I cannot make the bridge sound, and to hold anything I need two anchors in good rock. This mountain has one place that qualifies: the limestone knuckle where the ledge turns away. Four hours, perhaps.

**Roth**  
Perhaps.

**Illuminara**  
Plan for three.

He nodded like a man accepting an honest invoice. The track down was two and a half kilometres of ledge, single file, and its first four hundred metres ran under the slab's shadow before the cliff turned away. Sixty-two people lived in Kesk. Sixty-one were on the church green with their bags.

**Roth**  
The sixty-second has locked herself in the burial ground. The gate, I mean, with a key. The wall beside it fell down in 'ninety-eight.

scenes.title: The Circuit
paragraphs: *The burial ground above the church · half past twelve*

Ostrava Mehl was ninety-one and walked as though the ground were a sentence she was checking for errors. She went along the first row with a stick in one hand and a ring of iron keys in the other, and when Illuminara stepped through the gap where the wall had been, she did not look up.
Illuminara fell in beside her and said nothing for a full row. It was the most useful thing she had done all day. The old woman's lips were moving. She never repeated herself.
A man came up the path at a run and stopped with his hands on his knees. Davor Mehl was fifty, a quarry foreman, and the only person in Kesk who had ever been forgiven for raising his voice to her.

**Davor**  
Auntie. The captain says three hours at the outside.

**Ostrava**  
Then you have time to be quiet.

**Davor**  
You hold mountains, don't you? That is what they say. Then you can hold her. Put her over your shoulder and let us go, and she will thank you at ninety-five.

**Illuminara**  
It would work. That is what is wrong with it.
Ostrava stopped, for the first time, and looked at Illuminara properly, as one inspects a stranger who has said something unexpected.

**Illuminara**  
What are you saying?

**Ostrava**  
Names. Two hundred and fourteen, in the order they lie. Thirty-seven have no stone: the cough winter, the Pirc fire, the ones nobody could pay a mason for. There was a book. The school burned in 'seventy-four and the book went with it, and my mother gave me these keys and the order of the rows and said, whoever walks this after you walks it from you or not at all. I have been through it twice since the siren. I lose the order at the east wall.

**Illuminara**  
So you are not refusing to leave.

**Ostrava**  
I am refusing to leave them unsaid.

**Illuminara**  
How long does it take to say them all?

**Ostrava**  
Four hours, walking. I will not say a name I have not stood at.

**Davor**  
Auntie, nobody asked you that.

**Ostrava**  
Nobody asked me anything. They asked if I was coming. I did the sum myself, Davor, before you had your boots on. Four hours, and the track is an hour and a half. I chose the names.
Illuminara saw then that the village had spent the morning arguing with a refusal, and that no one had asked what it was for. Davor had gone the colour of the church wall. She let him.

scenes.title: Three Clocks
paragraphs: *The church porch · one in the afternoon*
They laid it out on the porch flags with Roth's tablet and a stub of builder's chalk, because it turned out to be three problems wearing one coat.

**Illuminara**  
The slab's clock: down by eight at the latest, sooner if the rain is early. The track's clock: three hours for sixty-two people, with the old and the stones. Ostrava's clock: four hours, because the list can only travel as fast as one pair of legs.

**Ostrava**  
Legs are what a person has.

**Illuminara**  
Then borrow more. The list is not slow. The walking is. Sit you in a chair at the crossing of the paths. Six people each take a row, walk to a grave, and stand at it. You say who lies there, from where you sit. A seventh writes. They have stood at the place, and you have heard them stand. Two hours, perhaps less.

**Ostrava**  
And when they stand at the wrong mound?

**Illuminara**  
Then you tell them, and they go to the right one. That is all a reading is.

**Ostrava**  
They will point at moles.

**Roth**  
Everyone who is not needed for the reading goes now, children first, and the bend belongs to them alone until they are across.

**Roth**  
Your hold starts when the slab tells us, not when it suits you. Anchors are a clock too. Four hours spent at noon are four hours you will not have at six.

**Roth**  
Then the ledge. The old trough stands two hundred metres in, under the slab. Short of the trough, if anything goes wrong, you turn back to the kiln cut: two metres of rock over it, and I have sat under it myself. Past the trough, the way out is forward. Nobody runs. A running line shakes the ledge.

**Davor**  
The geophone is mine. I listen to the cracking. Forty ticks a minute, or Illuminara tells me an anchor is going, and we do what the captain said, and whatever is unfinished stays where it is. Nobody argues.

**Illuminara**  
Your call, not mine. If it crosses forty, I am not an argument.

**Davor**  
And the sum, so I do not invent it on the day. From the trough to the knuckle is two hundred metres. A chair's pace covers that in five minutes, six on a bad step, and I want half as much again in hand for the last foot. Nine. At the trough I ask her for her hold. Nine or more, we pass it. Less, we take the kiln cut.

**Ostrava**  
Can you put it down somewhere else?

**Illuminara**  
No. It falls where the plane tilts. I can choose when. The when has to be after you are all out.

**Illuminara**  
The twelve line stones, the first stone of each row, are the oldest and the heaviest. I can lift them down the ledge myself.

**Ostrava**  
You will not. They go by sledge, on shoulders. Whoever carries them down will carry them again on All Souls. A stone that arrived by miracle is a stone nobody has to look after.
She was right, and she had made it a better plan. Illuminara wrote *sledges, shoulders* on the flags and underlined it.

**Ostrava**  
When the reading is done I will say them all again, from the chair, going down. Once to the ground, once to the six who stood on it.

**Ostrava**  
Davor. You will carry the register.

**Davor**  
Auntie, I will carry you.

**Ostrava**  
Not me. What I say. Lift that, and four of your neighbours may carry the rest of me, on the Pirc chair, because my own has a bad leg.
For a moment Davor looked as though he might refuse the whole arrangement out of pure relief. Then he took the tablet from Roth and held it as one holds something alive.

scenes.title: The Reading
paragraphs: *The limestone knuckle at the far end of the ledge · half past two*
The gauge touched twenty millimetres an hour at twenty-seven minutes past two, and Illuminara set both hands into the only sound rock on the mountain and took the slab's weight onto her own.

It was like lifting a table that a hundred people were leaning on. Roth stood beside her with a handset clipped to his collar and a face that offered nothing, which she was grateful for. Through the radio, from three hundred metres up the slope, came a kitchen chair scraping on gravel.

**Ostrava (radio)**  
Row one, from the church wall. Hedvig Mehl, who kept bees. Josef Brunec, who did not. Mara Pirc, four years old. Tomo, you are on her feet. Step back one.

**Davor (radio)**  
Written. Next.

Up the slope, through the bridge and into the shoulder, she could feel what the mountain remembered of two hundred and fourteen openings, each a small softness where hands had once dug and filled. She could have counted them. She could not have told one from another by anything but its depth, which was the whole point of the old woman and the whole trouble.
The names came across the gorge like a train of small carriages, each with someone in it. Row two. Row three.

**Ostrava (radio)**  
That is a mole, Brina.
The radio filled with six people trying not to laugh.

**Ostrava (radio)**  
East wall. Third mound.
The radio hissed. A minute went, and another. Under Illuminara's hands the north anchor shifted a hair, like a tooth.

**Ostrava (radio)**  
I had it this morning.

**Davor (radio)**  
Nan Pirc's boy. Teodor. He fell off the Pirc barn in 'fifty-one and Nan hauled a bench up here every Sunday till she died.

**Ostrava (radio)**  
Who told you that?

**Davor (radio)**  
You did. I was nine. You made me carry the bench.
There was a long hiss. Illuminara held the mountain and waited.

**Ostrava (radio)**  
Write it.
It was, she thought, the first name Ostrava had said in nine hours that she had not said alone.
At twenty past four the chair scraped for the last time. Row twelve was said, and the thirty-seven with no stone were pegged where the walkers had stood, each peg tied with a name.

**Ostrava (radio)**  
The count.

**Davor (radio)**  
Two hundred and fourteen. Thirty-seven pegs, and Brina has counted them twice. Every one is on the tablet against its row and its paces from the east wall.

**Ostrava (radio)**  
Read me the last peg.

**Davor (radio)**  
Jelka Pirc. The Pirc fire. Row twelve, three paces from the east wall.

**Roth**  
The valley station has the file. A second copy, off the mountain.

**Ostrava (radio)**  
Then it is out of my head. Good. It was getting heavy.

scenes.title: The Bend
paragraphs: *The far end of the ledge · twenty-five to six*

They came along the ledge in the last of the light, twenty-two lanterns in a line against a face the colour of slate: six sledges with the line stones lashed on, a chain of neighbours who had done this every All Souls of their lives, and in the middle, four of them carrying a kitchen chair with a very small woman sitting bolt upright in it. Davor walked at the back with the tablet inside his coat and the geophone in his hand.

Ostrava was saying them again, as she had promised, from row one. It had turned out that the register was in four-four time, and the bearers had fallen into step with it, a name to a stride, so that the chair rode level on the ledge.
At twenty to six the rock under Illuminara's left hand turned to grit.

**Illuminara**  
Roth. North anchor is gone. I am moving east. Eleven minutes at half strength.

**Roth**  
Say it to Davor.

**Illuminara**  
Davor. Eleven minutes, half strength.

**Davor (radio)**  
Thirty-four.
She slid her hand along the knuckle, found a seam, and leaned into it. The slab took a breath above them, and she felt it as a stranger's weight on her arm.

**Davor (radio)**  
Thirty-eight.

The tail of the line, Davor's lantern, had just come level with the trough, two hundred metres from her. *Forty,* she thought, *and the plan says the kiln cut or on, and his sum decides which.* She did not speak. It was his line.

**Davor (radio)**  
We are at the trough. Forward is six minutes on a bad step against her eleven, and the rule was nine. We pass it. Walk. Do not run. Running shakes the ledge.
Down the gorge came the old woman's voice, flat and steady, at the pace of a walk.

**Ostrava (radio)**  
Alois Vrh, a good man and a bad fiddler. Lena Vrh, who forgave him.

**Davor (radio)**  
Thirty-six.

At the third minute a sledge runner caught in a crack of the ledge and four men stood still for the length of a breath. It was the bad step the sum had allowed for. The line moved again, and nobody ran.

At four minutes the first sledge reached her, and the man hauling it said something to nobody that had the shape of a prayer, and kept going. At five the chair passed. Ostrava did not look at her. She was on row nine.

**Davor (radio)**  
Last foot clear.

**Roth**  
Six minutes.

**Illuminara**  
Then I am putting it down.

**Roth**  
Say it to someone who can answer.

**Illuminara**  
Ostrava. Is there anything the mountain still owes you?

**Ostrava (radio)**  
Nothing it can pay.

She lowered it. She did not drop it. For a moment the slab seemed to remember it was falling, as a person remembers a name, and then it went, and the shoulder opened and closed over two hundred and fourteen small softnesses all at once. She did not look away. The slab came down on empty ground.

scenes.title: East Corner
paragraphs: *The threshing terrace below Kesk · the next morning, frost*
Sixty-two people stood on the old threshing terrace with their breath hanging over them, and above them the mountain had a new face. Nobody said the word *cairn*. Nobody would for a year.

Davor had three printed copies of the register in a plastic sleeve: one for the diocese, one for the council, one for the cousins in Toronto. They had rung every All Souls and been told, correctly, that Aunt Rozalija lay at the top of the hill in the third row. This year they would be told, correctly, that she lay there still, under the mountain, and that her name would be cut in April at the east corner of the terrace below, where the living could stand. The register had two columns now, because Ostrava had insisted: where each of them lies, and where each is remembered. Twelve line stones stood in a row on the frosted grass. Beside Illuminara a woman called Brina, who had been wrong about the moles, put a cup of tea into her hands without asking. They shook a little. She let them.

**Davor**  
The council sat till two. The terrace is a memorial ground, not a graveyard. Nobody is moved, and nobody is to say they were. The thirty-seven are to be cut first, before any stone that already had one.

**Ostrava**  
I would have asked for that.

**Davor**  
You did not ask.

**Ostrava**  
I did not think it could be asked.

She stood up from the Pirc chair without help, took her stick in one hand and her keys in the other, and went along the terrace until she had found the corner she wanted. She put the Mehl line stone down herself and took her time over it.

**Ostrava**  
East corner. It gets the sun in the morning.

**Ostrava**  
You told me you could not put it down somewhere else.

**Illuminara**  
I could not.

**Ostrava**  
Then all you did was let it fall when we were ready. I do not forgive the mountain. I may forgive you by spring.
Davor, kneeling in the frost, wrote the corner's name at the top of a clean page.

critic_line: Illuminara understands that Ostrava is not refusing rescue but guarding an irreplaceable order of names, then helps the village distribute that memory without taking away anyone's authority; all sixty-two leave safely, all 214 names are recorded and the unmarked dead receive first priority in the memorial ground.

literary_score.method: READER_APPEAL_R1; genuine independent GPT and Claude judgments; exact equal 50/50 arithmetic mean.
shared_strengths: Humane, dialogue-heavy, with a clear ticking clock and a fresh idea: the names are the burden, so the village shares the carrying. The mole and Teodor moments are memorable. The logistics (three clocks, sums, rules) are a bit procedural, and the ending is quietly moving rather than a showstopper.

A gripping physical deadline is fused with a humane conflict about memory, duty, and consent. Distinctive dialogue, precise logistics, and cumulative emotional turns should sustain most readers, though the extended procedural planning may briefly slow momentum. The names, the coordinated crossing, and the final distinction between burial and remembrance are strongly memorable.
shared_reservations: The twelve line stones, the first stone of each row, are the oldest and the heaviest. I can lift them down the ledge myself.
Then the ledge. The old trough stands two hundred metres in, under the slab.

translation_sl.title: STARKA, KI NI HOTELA ZAPUSTITI GROBOV
translation_sl.deck: Plošča velikosti skednja se pomika proti vasi Kesk, najstarejša vaščanka pa se je zaklenila na pokopališče; Illuminara spozna, kaj varuje njena zavrnitev, vas pa najde način, da to odnese s seboj.
translation_sl.shape: Šest prizorov v enem popoldnevu in naslednjem jutru: tri ure reševalnega kapitana, hoja vzdolž pokopaliških vrst, načrt na cerkveni verandi, branje dvesto štirinajstih imen po radiu, prečkanje police pod popuščajočo ploščo in pomrznjena terasa, kjer postavijo prvi kamen.

scenes.title: Plošča
paragraphs: *Kesk, steza ob pečini · poldne*

Plošča nad Keskom je bila velika kakor skedenj in se je premikala že devet dni. Premikala se je tako, kakor se utrujen otrok nasloni na vrata, tako počasi, da nihče ni mogel reči, kdaj naslanjanje ni bilo več zgolj naslanjanje.

Kapitan Iven Roth iz dolinske reševalne službe je Illuminara poklical sam, in razumela je, da ga je to nekaj stalo. Ni ji segel v roko. Ponudil ji je tablico, kakor človek zdravniku pokaže rano, ki jo je že sam diagnosticiral.

**Roth**  
V ponedeljek dva milimetra na dan. Danes zjutraj enajst na uro. Če narišemo obratno vrednost hitrosti, se črta spusti do ničle približno ob osmih zvečer, plus ali minus tri ure. Ob osmih je napovedan dež. Sam sebi govorim, da ob sedmih.

Dlan je položila plosko na pečino ob stezi in pustila gori, da ji pokaže, kje se drži. Plošča ni visela s stene. Naslanjala se je na skalni most za seboj, na steber, širok kakor avtobus, preklan kakor kuhana kost, ki je opravljal delo celotnega pobočja. Čutila je, kako obremenitev teče skozenj, kakor se v zapestju čuti utrip.

**Illuminara**  
Težo plošče lahko prevzamem s tega mostu. Mostu ne morem narediti trdnega, za držanje česarkoli pa potrebujem dve sidri v zdravi skali. Na tej gori je samo eno ustrezno mesto: apnenčasti členek, kjer se polica odmakne. Morda štiri ure.

**Roth**  
Morda.

**Illuminara**  
Načrtujte za tri.

Pokimal je kakor človek, ki sprejema pošten račun. Pot navzdol je vodila dva kilometra in pol po ozki polici, v eni vrsti, njenih prvih štiristo metrov pa je teklo pod senco plošče, preden se je pečina odmaknila. V Kesku je živelo dvainšestdeset ljudi. Enainšestdeset jih je s prtljago čakalo na travniku pred cerkvijo.

**Roth**  
Dvainšestdeseta se je zaklenila na pokopališče. Mislim vrata, s ključem. Zid poleg njih se je podrl leta osemindevetdeset.

scenes.title: Obhod
paragraphs: *Pokopališče nad cerkvijo · pol enih*

Ostrava Mehl je imela enaindevetdeset let in hodila, kakor da so tla stavek, v katerem preverja napake. Pomikala se je vzdolž prve vrste s palico v eni roki in obročem železnih ključev v drugi, in ko je Illuminara stopila skozi vrzel, kjer je nekoč stal zid, ni dvignila pogleda.
Illuminara se ji je pridružila in vso prvo vrsto ni rekla ničesar. To je bilo najbolj koristno, kar je storila ves dan. Ustnice starke so se premikale. Nikoli se ni ponovila.
Po stezi je pritekel moški in obstal z rokami na kolenih. Davor Mehl je imel petdeset let, bil je delovodja v kamnolomu in edini človek v Kesku, ki mu je kdaj odpustila, da je povzdignil glas nanjo.

**Davor**  
Teta. Kapitan pravi, da imamo največ tri ure.

**Ostrava**  
Potem imaš čas, da si tiho.

**Davor**  
Gore držiš, kajne? Tako pravijo. Potem lahko držiš tudi njo. Daj si jo čez ramo, pa pojdimo, in zahvalila se ti bo pri petindevetdesetih.

**Illuminara**  
Delovalo bi. Prav v tem je težava.
Ostrava se je prvič ustavila in Illuminara zares pogledala, kakor človek premeri neznanca, ki je rekel nekaj nepričakovanega.

**Illuminara**  
Kaj govorite?

**Ostrava**  
Imena. Dvesto štirinajst, v vrstnem redu, v katerem ležijo. Sedemintrideset jih nima kamna: zima kašlja, požar pri Pirčevih, tisti, ki jim nihče ni mogel plačati kamnoseka. Bila je knjiga. Šola je zgorela leta štiriinsedemdeset in knjiga z njo, mati pa mi je dala te ključe in red vrst ter rekla: kdor bo to prehodil za teboj, bo prehodil po tvojem spominu ali pa sploh ne. Od sirene sem ga prehodila dvakrat. Pri vzhodnem zidu izgubim vrstni red.

**Illuminara**  
Torej ne zavračate odhoda.

**Ostrava**  
Zavračam, da bi jih zapustila neizgovorjene.

**Illuminara**  
Koliko časa traja, da izgovorite vsa imena?

**Ostrava**  
Štiri ure med hojo. Ne bom izrekla imena, pri katerem nisem stala.

**Davor**  
Teta, tega te nihče ni vprašal.

**Ostrava**  
Nihče me ni vprašal ničesar. Vprašali so me, ali grem. Sama sem izračunala, Davor, še preden si obul škornje. Štiri ure, pot pa uro in pol. Izbrala sem imena.
Illuminara je tedaj spoznala, da se je vas vse jutro prepirala z zavrnitvijo, nihče pa ni vprašal, kaj ta zavrnitev varuje. Davor je postal barve cerkvenega zidu. Pustila ga je.

scenes.title: Tri ure
paragraphs: *Cerkvena veranda · ena popoldne*
Razgrnili so ga na kamnitih ploščah verande z Rothovo tablico in koščkom zidarske krede, ker se je izkazalo, da gre za tri težave v enem plašču.

**Illuminara**  
Ura plošče: zgrmi najpozneje ob osmih, prej, če dež pohiti. Ura poti: tri ure za dvainšestdeset ljudi, skupaj s starimi in kamni. Ostravina ura: štiri ure, ker seznam lahko potuje le tako hitro kakor en par nog.

**Ostrava**  
Noge so tisto, kar človek ima.

**Illuminara**  
Potem si jih izposodite več. Seznam ni počasen. Počasna je hoja. Sedite na stol na križišču poti. Šest ljudi naj prevzame vsak svojo vrsto, hodi od groba do groba in ob vsakem obstane. Vi od tam, kjer sedite, poveste, kdo leži tam. Sedmi zapisuje. Oni so stali na kraju, vi pa ste jih slišali stati. Dve uri, morda manj.

**Ostrava**  
In ko bodo obstali pri napačni gomili?

**Illuminara**  
Potem jim poveste in gredo k pravi. To je vse, kar branje je.

**Ostrava**  
Kazali bodo na krtine.

**Roth**  
Vsi, ki jih pri branju ne potrebujemo, odidejo zdaj, najprej otroci, in zavoj pripada samo njim, dokler niso čez.

**Roth**  
Držati začneš, ko nam to pove plošča, ne ko tebi ustreza. Tudi sidra imajo svojo uro. Štiri ure, porabljene opoldne, so štiri ure, ki jih ob šestih ne boš imela.

**Roth**  
Potem polica. Staro korito stoji dvesto metrov naprej, pod ploščo. Pred koritom se ob vsaki težavi obrnete nazaj proti useku pri peči: nad njim sta dva metra skale in sam sem že sedel pod njo. Za koritom vodi pot samo še naprej. Nihče ne teče. Tekoča kolona trese polico.

**Davor**  
Geofon je moj. Poslušam pokanje. Štirideset sunkov na minuto, ali pa Illuminara pove, da sidro popušča, in naredimo, kar je rekel kapitan; kar še ni končano, ostane tam. Nihče se ne prepira.

**Illuminara**  
Odločitev je tvoja, ne moja. Če preseže štirideset, jaz nisem argument.

**Davor**  
In še račun, da si ga ne bom izmišljal na sam dan. Od korita do členka je dvesto metrov. S stolom prehodimo to v petih minutah, šestih na slabem koraku, za zadnjega človeka pa hočem še polovico toliko rezerve. Devet. Pri koritu jo vprašam, koliko časa lahko drži. Devet ali več in gremo naprej. Manj in gremo v usek pri peči.

**Ostrava**  
Jo lahko odložiš kam drugam?

**Illuminara**  
Ne. Pade tja, kamor je nagnjena drsna ploskev. Izberem lahko kdaj. Ta kdaj mora biti po tem, ko ste vsi zunaj.

**Illuminara**  
Dvanajst vrstnih kamnov, prvi kamen vsake vrste, je najstarejših in najtežjih. Sama jih lahko odnesem po polici navzdol.

**Ostrava**  
Ne boš jih. Gredo na saneh, na ramenih. Kdor jih odnese dol, jih bo spet nosil na vse svete. Za kamen, ki je prispel po čudežu, ni treba nikomur skrbeti.
Imela je prav in načrt je zaradi nje postal boljši. Illuminara je na kamnite plošče zapisala *sani, ramena* in besedi podčrtala.

**Ostrava**  
Ko bo branje končano, jih bom vse povedala še enkrat, s stola, med potjo navzdol. Enkrat tlom, enkrat šestim, ki so stali na njih.

**Ostrava**  
Davor. Ti boš nesel register.

**Davor**  
Teta, jaz bom nesel tebe.

**Ostrava**  
Ne mene. To, kar povem. Dvigni to, štirje tvoji sosedje pa lahko na Pirčevem stolu odnesejo še preostanek mene, ker ima moj zlomljeno nogo.
Za trenutek je bil Davor videti, kakor da bi utegnil iz samega olajšanja zavrniti celoten dogovor. Nato je Rothu vzel tablico in jo držal, kakor človek drži nekaj živega.

scenes.title: Branje
paragraphs: *Apnenčasti členek na skrajnem koncu police · pol treh*
Merilnik je ob sedemindvajset minut čez dve dosegel dvajset milimetrov na uro in Illuminara je obe roki zasidrala v edino zdravo skalo na gori ter težo plošče prevzela nase.

Bilo je kakor dvigniti mizo, na katero se opira sto ljudi. Roth je stal ob njej s slušalko, pripeto na ovratnik, in obrazom, ki ni razkrival ničesar, za kar mu je bila hvaležna. Po radiu, s tristo metrov višjega pobočja, je prišlo drsenje kuhinjskega stola po produ.

**Ostrava (radio)**  
Prva vrsta, od cerkvenega zidu. Hedvig Mehl, ki je gojila čebele. Josef Brunec, ki jih ni. Mara Pirc, štiri leta. Tomo, stojiš ji na nogah. Stopi korak nazaj.

**Davor (radio)**  
Zapisano. Naslednji.

Navzgor po pobočju, skozi most in v ramo gore je lahko čutila, kaj si gora pomni o dvesto štirinajstih odprtinah, vsaki majhni mehkobi, kjer so roke nekoč kopale in zasipavale. Lahko bi jih preštela. Med seboj jih ne bi mogla ločiti po ničemer razen po globini, in prav v tem sta bila ves smisel starke in vsa težava.
Imena so prihajala čez sotesko kakor vlak majhnih vagonov, v vsakem je nekdo sedel. Druga vrsta. Tretja vrsta.

**Ostrava (radio)**  
To je krtina, Brina.
Radio je napolnil zvok šestih ljudi, ki so se trudili, da se ne bi zasmejali.

**Ostrava (radio)**  
Vzhodni zid. Tretja gomila.
Radio je zašumel. Minila je minuta, nato še ena. Pod Illuminarinima rokama se je severno sidro premaknilo za las, kakor zob.

**Ostrava (radio)**  
Zjutraj sem vedela.

**Davor (radio)**  
Fant Nan Pirc. Teodor. Leta enainpetdeset je padel s Pirčevega skednja in Nan je vsako nedeljo, dokler ni umrla, sem gor vlekla klop.

**Ostrava (radio)**  
Kdo ti je to povedal?

**Davor (radio)**  
Ti. Imel sem devet let. Prisilila si me nositi klop.
Dolgo je šumelo. Illuminara je držala goro in čakala.

**Ostrava (radio)**  
Zapiši.
To je bilo, je pomislila, prvo ime, ki ga je Ostrava v devetih urah izrekla, ne da bi ga izrekla sama.

Ob dvajset čez štiri je stol zadnjič podrsal. Dvanajsta vrsta je bila izrečena, ob sedemintridesetih brez kamna pa so zabili količke tam, kjer so stali bralci, na vsakem količku je bilo privezano ime.

**Ostrava (radio)**  
Število.

**Davor (radio)**  
Dvesto štirinajst. Sedemintrideset količkov, Brina jih je preštela dvakrat. Vsak je na tablici zapisan ob svoji vrsti in številu korakov od vzhodnega zidu.

**Ostrava (radio)**  
Preberi mi zadnji količek.

**Davor (radio)**  
Jelka Pirc. Požar pri Pirčevih. Dvanajsta vrsta, tri korake od vzhodnega zidu.

**Roth**  
Dolinska postaja ima datoteko. Drugi izvod, zunaj gore.

**Ostrava (radio)**  
Potem ni več samo v moji glavi. Dobro. Postajalo je težko.

scenes.title: Zavoj
paragraphs: *Skrajni konec police · petindvajset minut do šestih*

Po polici so prišli v zadnji svetlobi, dvaindvajset svetilk v vrsti ob steni barve skrilavca: šest sani s privezanimi vrstnimi kamni, veriga sosedov, ki so to počeli ob vseh svetih vse svoje življenje, sredi njih pa štirje, ki so nosili kuhinjski stol, na katerem je vzravnano sedela zelo majhna ženska. Davor je hodil zadaj s tablico pod plaščem in geofonom v roki.

Ostrava jih je, kakor je obljubila, znova izgovarjala od prve vrste naprej. Izkazalo se je, da je register v štiričetrtinskem taktu, nosači pa so svoj korak prilagodili ritmu, eno ime na korak, zato je stol po polici potoval naravnost.
Dvajset minut do šestih se je skala pod Illuminarino levo roko spremenila v drobir.

**Illuminara**  
Roth. Severno sidro je odpovedalo. Pomikam se proti vzhodu. Enajst minut s polovično močjo.

**Roth**  
Povej Davorju.

**Illuminara**  
Davor. Enajst minut, polovična moč.

**Davor (radio)**  
Štiriintrideset.
Z roko je zdrsnila vzdolž členka, našla šiv in se uprla vanj. Plošča je nad njimi vdihnila in začutila jo je kakor težo tujca na svoji roki.

**Davor (radio)**  
Osemintrideset.

Rep kolone, Davorjeva svetilka, je pravkar dosegel korito, dvesto metrov od nje. *Štirideset,* je pomislila, *načrt pa pravi usek pri peči ali naprej, njegov račun odloči, kaj.* Ni spregovorila. Kolona je bila njegova.

**Davor (radio)**  
Pri koritu smo. Naprej je šest minut ob slabem koraku proti njenim enajstim, pravilo pa je bilo devet. Gremo naprej. Hodite. Ne tecite. Tek trese polico.
Po soteski navzdol je prihajal starkin glas, raven in miren, v ritmu hoje.

**Ostrava (radio)**  
Alois Vrh, dober človek in slab godec. Lena Vrh, ki mu je odpustila.

**Davor (radio)**  
Šestintrideset.
V tretji minuti se je drsnik sani zataknil v razpoko police in štirje moški so obstali za en dih. To je bil slab korak, ki ga je račun dopuščal. Kolona se je znova premaknila in nihče ni tekel.

V četrti minuti so jo dosegle prve sani, moški, ki jih je vlekel, pa je nikomur izrekel nekaj, kar je imelo obliko molitve, in nadaljeval. Ob petih minutah je šel mimo stol. Ostrava je ni pogledala. Bila je pri deveti vrsti.

**Davor (radio)**  
Zadnji človek je zunaj.

**Roth**  
Šest minut.

**Illuminara**  
Potem jo bom odložila.

**Roth**  
Povej nekomu, ki lahko odgovori.

**Illuminara**  
Ostrava. Ali vam gora še kaj dolguje?

**Ostrava (radio)**  
Ničesar, kar bi lahko plačala.

Spustila jo je. Ni je izpustila. Za trenutek se je zdelo, da se plošča spominja, da pada, kakor se človek spomni imena, nato pa je zdrsnila in gorska rama se je hkrati odprla in zaprla nad dvesto štirinajstimi majhnimi mehkobami. Ni pogledala stran. Plošča je padla na prazna tla.

scenes.title: Vzhodni kot
paragraphs: *Mlatilna terasa pod Keskom · naslednje jutro, slana*
Dvainšestdeset ljudi je stalo na stari mlatilni terasi, njihov dih je visel nad njimi, gora pa je imela nov obraz. Nihče ni izrekel besede *gomila*. Nihče je ne bo še eno leto.

Davor je imel v plastični mapi tri natisnjene izvode registra: enega za škofijo, enega za občino in enega za sorodnike v Torontu. Vsako leto ob vseh svetih so poklicali in izvedeli, pravilno, da teta Rozalija leži na vrhu hriba v tretji vrsti. Letos jim bodo povedali, prav tako pravilno, da še vedno leži tam, pod goro, njeno ime pa bodo aprila vklesali v vzhodni kot spodnje terase, kjer lahko stojijo živi. Register je imel zdaj dva stolpca, ker je Ostrava vztrajala: kje vsak od njih leži in kje se vsakega spominjajo. Dvanajst vrstnih kamnov je stalo v vrsti na pomrznjeni travi. Ob Illuminari ji je ženska po imenu Brina, tista, ki se je motila glede krtin, brez vprašanja položila skodelico čaja v roke. Roke so se ji malo tresle. Pustila jim je.

**Davor**  
Svet je zasedal do dveh. Terasa je spominski prostor, ne pokopališče. Nihče ni bil premaknjen in nihče ne sme reči, da je bil. Najprej bo vklesanih sedemintrideset, pred vsakim, ki je že imel kamen.

**Ostrava**  
To bi prosila.

**Davor**  
Nisi prosila.

**Ostrava**  
Nisem pomislila, da bi lahko.
Brez pomoči je vstala s Pirčevega stola, vzela palico v eno roko in ključe v drugo ter šla vzdolž terase, dokler ni našla želenega kota. Sama je odložila vrstni kamen Mehlovih in si vzela čas.

**Ostrava**  
Vzhodni kot. Zjutraj ga obsije sonce.

**Ostrava**  
Rekla si mi, da je ne moreš odložiti drugam.

**Illuminara**  
Nisem je mogla.

**Ostrava**  
Potem si jo samo pustila pasti, ko smo bili pripravljeni. Gori ne odpustim. Tebi morda odpustim do pomladi.
Davor je, klečeč v slani, na vrh čiste strani zapisal ime kota.

translation_sl.critic_line: Illuminara razume, da Ostrava ne zavrača rešitve, temveč varuje nenadomestljivi red imen, nato pa vasi pomaga razdeliti ta spomin, ne da bi komurkoli odvzela avtoriteto; vseh dvainšestdeset ljudi varno odide, vseh 214 imen je zapisanih, neoznačeni mrtvi pa dobijo prednost v spominskem prostoru.
